definitions.explanation: A married couple who are both elderly. Often used warmly to describe a couple who have been together for a long time.

examples.japanese: {老夫婦|ろうふうふ}が{手|て}をつないで{歩|ある}いていた。
examples.english: An elderly couple was walking hand in hand.

examples.japanese: {隣|となり}に{住|す}む{老夫婦|ろうふうふ}はとても{仲|なか}がいい。
examples.english: The elderly couple living next door get along very well.

examples.japanese: その{老夫婦|ろうふうふ}は{五十|ごじゅう}{年|ねん}{以上|いじょう}も{一緒|いっしょ}に{暮|く}らしてきたそうだ。
examples.english: I hear that elderly couple has lived together for over fifty years.

notes:
{老夫婦|ろうふうふ} refers to a married couple who are both elderly, typically implying they have been together for many years.

FORMS:
{老|ろう} (old, elderly) + {夫婦|ふうふ} (married couple).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {老夫婦|ろうふうふ}が{暮|く}らす: an elderly couple lives (together)
- {仲|なか}のいい{老夫婦|ろうふうふ}: a close/loving elderly couple
- {老夫婦|ろうふうふ}{二人暮|ふたりぐ}らし: an elderly couple living alone together

USAGE:
Generally a neutral or warm term. In stories and narratives, {老夫婦|ろうふうふ} often evokes long companionship, quiet lives, or touching devotion. It appears frequently in folktales (e.g., おじいさんとおばあさん scenes).

RELATED WORDS:
- {夫婦|ふうふ}: married couple (general)
- {若夫婦|わかふうふ}: young married couple
- {新婚|しんこん}{夫婦|ふうふ}: newlywed couple
- {老人|ろうじん}: elderly person (individual)
